title: US Civil Rights Movement 1954-1968
welcome_lead: From Brown v. Board to the assassination of Dr King, walk through the campaigns that transformed American citizenship.
meta_desc: History Rights & Protest Adventure 1: US Civil Rights Movement, 1954-1968.
final_note: You have followed the long road from Montgomery to Memphis. The unfinished business of civil rights endures.

walkthroughs.body_html: Brown v. Board of Education overturned the 'separate but equal' doctrine of Plessy v. Ferguson (1896). Massive resistance in the South — including the Little Rock Crisis of 1957 — followed. Rosa Parks' arrest in Montgomery (1 December 1955) galvanised a year-long bus boycott led by the young Reverend Martin Luther King Jr.

Student sit-ins (Greensboro 1960), Freedom Rides (1961) and the Birmingham campaign (1963) exposed segregation's brutality to a national television audience. Bull Connor's use of dogs and fire hoses helped shift opinion. The March on Washington in August 1963 pressed for federal legislation.

The Selma to Montgomery marches of March 1965 led directly to the Voting Rights Act. Tensions over poverty, Vietnam and Northern de facto segregation followed. Riots in Watts (1965), Newark and Detroit (1967), the rise of Black Power and the assassination of Dr King in Memphis on 4 April 1968 closed a transformative era.

mcqs.q: Why was the monarchy restored in 1660?
options: Parliament voted to restore the monarchy because Cromwell had taxed them too heavily.
Charles II invaded England with a French army and seized the throne.
Détente meant the USSR converted to capitalism.
After Cromwell's death the Protectorate collapsed; General Monck negotiated Charles II's return on the terms of the Declaration of Breda (amnesty, religious flexibility, army pay).

mcqs.q: Why did the superpowers pursue détente in the 1970s?
options: Détente meant the USSR converted to capitalism.
Détente ended the Cold War in the 1970s.
Mutual recognition of nuclear parity, US exhaustion from Vietnam, Soviet economic stagnation, and the cost of the arms race — formalised in SALT and the Helsinki Accords.
Parliament voted to restore the monarchy because Cromwell had taxed them too heavily.

mcqs.q: Why is Magna Carta still cited in 'Power and the People' history?
options: Parliament voted to restore the monarchy because Cromwell had taxed them too heavily.
Magna Carta directly created modern human rights in 1215.
Because clauses on lawful judgement and protection from arbitrary imprisonment were reinterpreted in the 17th century to support broader liberties, even though they originally protected only barons.
Magna Carta gave the right to vote to all English men.
